summary: Wenjie Duan (1917–2011) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at the Central Academy of Fine Arts (~1940–1943) and served as Director of the Dunhuang Academy in 1991.

Wenjie Qin is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. Qin earned a PhD at Harvard University, studying under doctoral supervisor Tu Weiming and teachers Diana L. Eck, Masatoshi Nagatomi, Charles Hallisey, and Robert M. Gimello.
Werner Abraham (1936–2024) was a linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (1962–1965). He held a post at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich in 2002.
Wes Borton works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Borton studied at East Carolina University, where Derek F. Maher was a teacher, and at the University of Michigan (attested 2010).

Whalen Lai (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He studied at International Christian University (~1965–1969) and Harvard University (~1970–1975). He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (attested 1993) and UC Davis (attested 2009).

Whitney Cox is an Indologist who studied at the University of Virginia (~1994–1998) and at the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~2000–2006). Cox also held a post at the University of Chicago (attested 2003).

Wilburn Hansen is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. Hansen completed a master's program at the University of Colorado Boulder and studied at Stanford University under teachers Bernard Faure and Carl Bielefeldt.

Wilfred Cantwell Smith (1916–2000) was a religious studies scholar. Educated at Upper Canada College (~1928–1934), the University of Toronto (~1934–1938), and Princeton University (~1944–1948), he served as director (所長) at Harvard University (~1964–1973).

Wilfrid Sellars (1912–1989) was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Montaigne, Michigan, Buffalo, Oriel College, and Göttingen. He held posts at Iowa (1938–1946), Minnesota (1947–1958), Yale (1958–1963), Pittsburgh (1963–1989), and Humboldt University of Berlin.

Wilhelm Deecke (1831–1897) was a linguist. He studied at the Katharineum, Leipzig, and Berlin under Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, and Moriz Haupt. He held posts at the Katharineum (1852–1855) and Ernestinenschule (1855–1870).

Wilhelm Geiger (1856–1943) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Erlangen-Nuremberg under Friedrich von Spiegel and at Bonn. He held positions at Erlangen-Nuremberg and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

Wilhelm Grube (1855–1908) was a sinologist and linguist. He studied under Vasily Vasiliev and at Leipzig University under Georg von der Gabelentz. He served as professor at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1892–1908).

Wilhelm Halbfass (1940–2000) was an Indologist and philosopher. He held academic posts at the University of Göttingen (~1968–1970), the University of Pennsylvania (~1973–2000), the University of Hamburg (1981–1982), and Wissenschaftskolleg zu Berlin (~1990–1991).

Wilhelm Pertsch (1832–1899) was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Weber in 1850, at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1853–1854), and under Rudolf von Roth (~1854–1855).

Wilhelm Rau (1922–1999) worked in Indology and linguistics. He held academic appointments at Leipzig University (~1948–1950), Goethe University Frankfurt (~1955–1957), and the University of Marburg (~1957–1988).

Wilhelm Scherer (1841–1886) was a scholar of linguistics. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1858–1860) and held posts at the University of Vienna (~1868–1872) and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1877–1886).

Wilhelm Schulze (1863–1935) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Marburg (~1892–1895), the University of Göttingen (~1895–1902), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1902–1932).

Wilhelm Streitberg (1864–1925) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leipzig University (~1884–1888). He held posts at the University of Münster (~1899–1909), Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1909–1920), and Leipzig University (~1920–1925).
Wilhelm Wackernagel (1806–1869) was a linguistics scholar. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1824–1827) and held a post at the University of Basel (~1833–1869).

Wilhelm von Humboldt (1767–1835) worked in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Frankfurt an der Oder, Göttingen, and Jena. He founded Humboldt University of Berlin in 1810 and held a post there from ~1810 to 1835.
